message.content: {"criteria":[{"id":"C1","level":"Adequate","mark":6,"evidence":[{"where":"Mission Concept & Rationale","quote":"A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events."},{"where":"Mission Concept & Rationale","quote":"This tool could be applied to a new satellite over the Great Barrier Reef."}],"reasoning":"Rationale and users (reef scientists, conservation managers, reliant communities) are clearly argued and referenced with footnotes. However, mission objectives and quantitative requirements (resolution, revisit, data latency, payload) are missing, and the users are only loosely specified. Adequate, upper end limited by the absent requirements."},{"id":"C2","level":"Adequate","mark":5,"evidence":[{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","quote":"Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart."},{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","quote":"In addition to my own research, the syllabus work on astrodynamics will help me to understand and design an optimal mission."}],"reasoning":"A week-by-week Gantt chart with tasks, deadlines and a final due date is provided, and sources are indicated. Detail is adequate and feasibility is credible, but there is no explicit contingency or variation planning and sources are not formally listed."},{"id":"C3","level":"Adequate","mark":4,"evidence":[{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","quote":"completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4."},{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","quote":"My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km"}],"reasoning":"Only minor progress is reported: reading, background research and tutorials. No simulation outputs, calculations or design results are presented, so the evidence of technical progress is thin. The orbit stated is technically incorrect, which undermines the progress claim."},{"id":"C4","level":"Accomplished","mark":8,"evidence":[{"where":"Mission Concept & Rationale","quote":"Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic since the industrial revolution leading to the bleaching of coral reefs.¹"},{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","quote":"Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines."}],"reasoning":"Clear headed structure, readable prose, footnoted references and a labelled Gantt chart with a legend. Some informal phrasing (\"maybe\", \"Need to decide\") and a mismatch between the 'Mission concept' and the Gantt legend keep it below top quality. Level ranges given (0–10) are used; the stated 20-mark weight is not reconciled with them."}],"requirements":[{"id":"R1","met":"partial","where":"Mission Concept & Rationale"},{"id":"R2","met":"partial","where":"Orbit Specifics"},{"id":"R3","met":"partial","where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress"},{"id":"R4","met":"yes","where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress"},{"id":"R5","met":"partial","where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress"},{"id":"R6","met":"partial","where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress"}],"technical_issues":[{"where":"Orbit Specifics","issue":"A geostationary orbit is at about 35,786 km altitude, not 600 km. A 600 km orbit cannot be geostationary, and it cannot keep a satellite fixed over the reef."},{"where":"Orbit Specifics","issue":"Claim that the satellite stays 'fixed above the reef at all times' is incorrect for any orbit at 600 km; ground track and coverage analysis are needed instead."},{"where":"Mission Concept & Rationale","issue":"Stated 'near-real-time' relay and revisit requirements are not quantified or linked to a link budget or orbit design."},{"where":"Project Plan & Preliminary Progress","issue":"Software choice (STK) is implied via tutorials but not explicitly stated as the selected package for the design."}],"overall":"A clearly motivated mission with a readable report and a usable Gantt chart. Weaknesses are the absence of quantified mission requirements, no technical results, and a serious orbit error (a 600 km geostationary orbit). Preliminary technical progress must be demonstrated with actual calculations or STK outputs. Level ranges (0–10) are inconsistent with stated criterion weights; marks are given within level ranges."}
